meta.dialect: Rigol DHO800/DHO900 subset with OOS extensions

intro: This chapter describes every command OOS Plus implements, grouped by subsystem. Commands marked **OOS** are extensions that the Rigol DHO800/DHO900 command set does not have. Commands not listed here are not supported and report error -113.

intro.p: The IEEE 488.2 common commands: identification, reset, the status registers (`*STB?`, `*ESE`, `*SRE`, `*ESR?`) and the operation-complete fence, plus `*SAV` and `*RCL`, which save and recall a numbered setup slot. `*OPC?` waits only for finite operations (Autoset, a submitted SIM generation, an armed Single); continuous Run and background analysis are not drained. `*SAV` and `*RCL` use the same files as Storage > Setup slot, so they are cross-linked from storage.
Menu location: Run control > Default setup; Storage > Save setup, Recall setup.
Part of the SCPI reference.

subsystems.title: System: Diagnostics, schema and setup block

intro.p: Everything under the System menu: identification text, the key = value setup schema, the whole-setup block, date, time and NTP, Ethernet and WLAN, the remote services switches, the scope name, touch lock, the quick key and session, and the commands that power off, restart, update, roll back or change the boot mode. Destructive commands take a literal `CONFIRM` argument and are refused with -221 without it; a command that would change nothing (the boot mode it already has) needs none. `:SYSTem:SETup` (long form) is the setup block; the short form `:SYST:SET` stays the older key = value command. The key list behind `:SYSTem:SET` is in setup keys.
Menu location: System (About, System info, Date and time, Network, Remote services, Update, Power), Run control > Power off / restart, Display and layout > Graphics.
Part of the SCPI reference.

commands.desc: Sets or queries Recall setup for Diagnostics, schema and setup block (menu: Storage > Recall setup).
params: Set: apply a setup block (or the plain text); the acquisition state stays as it is. The short form `:SYST:SET` is the key = value command.
commands.returns: Query: the whole setup (the file Save setup writes) as an IEEE block.

commands.desc: The setup as SCPI commands, as an IEEE block of lines: `*RST`, then one command for every setting that differs from the Default setup, each with the answer of its own query as the value. A setting without a header of its own is a `:SYSTem:SET` line; the headers are in the Equivalent header column of setup keys. Sent line by line to a scope, it brings that scope to this setup. Reference waveforms and notes are not part of it. A value with a `;` in it (a floating panel of the Studio layout) cannot travel in a line: it is left out and error -221 names its key. `SETup` is spelled out, as for `:SYSTem:SETup`.
remarks: - Menu equivalent: Storage > Save setup as SCPI.

- Origin: OOS extension. The first part of the SCPI recorder. The menu row writes the same lines to a new file where Storage saves, `setup-NNN.scpi` (`setup-<date>-<time>.scpi` once the clock is set).

commands.desc: Sets or queries SCPI recorder for Diagnostics, schema and setup block (menu: Storage > SCPI recorder).
remarks: - The SCPI recorder on or off, taken at the next frame.

- While it is on, what is set at the scope (touch, keys, knobs, menus) is written as commands: a setting is written when it has stood still for 0.6 s, so a knob that was turned is one line with the value it was left at.
- What a client sets by SCPI is not recorded: a comment in the file says where a client set something, and the file does not bring that.
- What the web remote's keys and touches do is recorded, as the front panel's.

- The lines go into a new file `recording-NNN.scpi` where Storage saves, written again after every step, so a recording is not lost when the program ends while it is on (a power cut is another matter: the local folder is in memory, and on a stick the file is certain only once the recorder was switched off); it ends by itself at 20000 lines.

- A key or a row that is an action is written as its command, with what was set before it first (before Default that is only the text size and the Quick key action, which Default leaves alone): Run / Stop (`:RUN`, `:STOP`), Single (`:SINGle`), Force (`:TFORce`), Clear (`:CLEar`), Default (`*RST`), Autoset (`:AUToscale`), and the Storage rows Save setup, Save waveform and Save screenshot (`*SAV <n>`, `:SAVE:WAVeform`, `:SAVE:IMAGe`).
- Save setup is written with its slot, which is not part of the setup: a replay writes the same slot and leaves the Setup slot row at it.
- The settings an action changes are its own and are not written as settings; an auto set-up is the command alone, so a replay finds what the signal then has.
- Recall setup and a loaded session are written as the settings they bring.
- Origin: OOS extension. The proof of every step is the one of `:SYSTem:SETup:SCPI?`.
commands.returns: On a freshly started default model the query returns `0`.

commands.desc: The lines of the recording that runs, else of the last one, as an IEEE block: comment lines (`#`), the setup at the start as commands (`*RST` and what differs from the Default setup), then the recorded commands, each step under a comment with its time (`# +12.4 s`). A setting that has not stood still yet is not in it. Empty before the first recording.

subsystems.title: Run control and acquisition: Run control

intro.p: Run, stop, single, autoset and clear; the acquisition type, averages, memory depth and the segmented frame count; and the history of stored acquisitions. There is one acquisition context: a loaded reference beside live channels is a passive overlay, and selecting a reference as the primary trigger source enters stored-record acquisition. `:RUN` and `:STOP` are assignments, so repeating either does not toggle it.
Menu location: Run control (Run / Stop, Single, Autoset, Clear), Acquisition (Mode, Averages, Memory depth, Segments), Run control > History.
Part of the SCPI reference.

commands.desc: Sets or queries Memory for Acquisition (menu: Acquire > Memory).
params: Set `AUTO` or a supported menu depth, e.g. `1000000`, `1M` (1k, 10k, 100k, 1M, 10M, 25M, 50M, 62.5M, 100M, 125M; what the unit has is cut to its memory). In roll mode (Auto Roll on and 200 ms/div or slower; stock rolls from 50) the record is the stream's points of the screen whatever the depth: the depth is kept for the faster time bases and the set is answered with -221 that names the depth, the reason and the way out (`:TIMebase:ROLL OFF`, or a time base faster than 200 ms/div). A value that is none of them is -224, and the error names the depths this unit takes (`5M` is none of them).

intro.p: The vertical settings of the analogue inputs `CHANnel<n>` (n = 1 to the number of channels of the model), and the selected channel. Scales are chosen at the nearest supported step and the probe factor applies. Waveform names in scripts are `CHAN1` to `CHAN4`, not the UI label `CH1`. Probe deskew (`:CHANnel<n>:TCALibrate`) is separate from the analysis deskew in calibration.
Menu location: Channels (Display, Scale, Offset, Coupling, Bandwidth limit, Probe ratio, Invert, Unit, Fine scale, Deskew, Zero bias, Expand around, Name).
Part of the SCPI reference.

intro.p: Trigger type, sweep, source and level, and one subsection per trigger type. The typed subtrees set the same fields as the menu pages (and the `:SYSTem:SET trig_*` keys); they do not change the trigger type, `:TRIGger:MODE` does. Times are seconds, 1 ns to 10 s. Pulse width conditions, slope and delay times, the window time, the runt width and the duration times share two fields: "lower" (`WIDTh`, `LWIDth`, `TIME`, `TLOWer`, `WLOWer`) is the menu's Time and "upper" (`UWIDth`, `TUPPer`, `WUPPer`) its Upper limit. Source and level of every type are `:TRIGger:EDGE:SOURce`, `:TRIGger:SOURce2` and `:TRIGger:EDGE:LEVel` (also `:TRIGger:<type>:SOURce`). Reference triggering is a software search over the stored samples; SIM cannot qualify LA, Pattern or Duration inputs.
Menu location: Trigger (Type, Source, Level, Slope, Sweep, Holdoff, Coupling, Noise reject and the page of each type).
Part of the SCPI reference.

after.p: BYTE is unsigned 8-bit. WORD is unsigned **little-endian** 16-bit, an explicit OOS wire policy (Rigol does not specify the byte order, so this is not a verified Rigol claim). ASCII is comma-separated volts in seven-significant-digit scientific notation; do not scale it again. `:WAVeform:DATA?` returns an IEEE definite-length block `#<N><N digits of length><payload>` followed by a newline: read the announced length, never split on newlines inside a payload. Pages whose worst-case encoded size exceeds 64 MiB are refused with -223. Stop acquisition first when metadata and data must match.

after.p: The canonical long spellings are accepted case-insensitively, as is the short form of the mixed-case spelling (for example `FREQ`, `RTIM`, `PWID`). The strip and readout print the canonical spelling. Aliases: `CYCAmp` = `CAMP`, `CYCPP` = `CPP`, `UI` = `ESTUI`, `LINSLOPE` = `LSLO`, `LININT` = `LINT`, `L0` to `L3` = `PAM0` to `PAM3`, `ONES` = `BITS`.
### Standard measurement items

`VPP`, `VMAX`, `VMIN`, `VAVG`, `VRMS`, `VAMP`, `FREQUENCY`, `PERIOD`, `RTIME`, `FTIME`, `PWIDTH`, `PDUTY`, `NDUTY`, `NWIDTH`, `VTOP`, `VBASE`, `OVERSHOOT`, `PRESHOOT`, `HTIME`, `LTIME`, `BWIDTH`, `TOUTSIDE`, `NPERIODS`, `CAMP`, `CTOP`, `CBASE`, `CPP`, `CMAX`, `CMIN`, `VUPPER`, `VMID`, `VLOWER`, `CAVG`, `CRMS`, `ACRMS`, `SDEVIATION`, `AREA`, `CAREA`, `PPULSES`, `NPULSES`, `PEDGES`, `NEDGES`, `TVMAX`, `TVMIN`, `PSLEW`, `NSLEW`, `ESTUI`, `MEDIAN`, `MODE`, `LSLO`, `LINT`, `PAM0`, `PAM1`, `PAM2`, `PAM3`, `PSEP`, `BITS`, `PLLUI`, `UIWTD`, `FOLD`.
### Pair items

`RRDELAY`, `FFDELAY`, `RFDELAY`, `FRDELAY`, `RRPHASE`, `FFPHASE`, `RFPHASE`, `FRPHASE`, `RRSKEW`, `FFSKEW`, `RFSKEW`, `FRSKEW`, `SETUP`, `HOLD`, `SETHOLD`, `FSETUP`, `FHOLD`, `DSETUP`, `DHOLD`, `DSETHOLD`.

Setup and hold take source A as the data and B as the clock, as on the measurement page (the order of the stock setup/hold trigger, which names the data source `:TRIGger:SHOLd:DSRC` before the clock `CSRC`; the stock `:MEASure:ITEM` has no setup or hold item). `SETUP`/`HOLD` latch on rising clock edges, `FSETUP`/`FHOLD` on falling ones, and the `D` items on both, as a DDR strobe (DQS) does. A clock edge counts only when the data changed inside its own cycle: after the previous latching edge and within one typical edge spacing. Data that holds steady between strobe bursts adds no setup or hold. `SETHOLD`/`DSETHOLD` count the edges that break `:MEASure:TSETup`/`:MEASure:THOLd`.
### Catalogue rows

The six-tab catalogue's selected rows are exported by `:MEASure:STRip?` and `:MEASure:READout?` as `CAT<id>,A,B,C,D,value`, including unused stored role columns. Add and query them with `:MEASure:CATalog:ITEM`; the per-row settings card stays on the setup key `row_cfg`.
### Analysis item families

The other analyser pages have their own `:ITEM?` queries: `:POWer:ITEM?`, `:SPECtrum:ITEM?` (spectrum), `:MAGnetic:ITEM?`, `:INVerter:ITEM?`, `:DPT:ITEM?` (power), `:BANDwidth:ITEM?` (bode) and `:EYE:ITEM?` (eye). See reference analysis for sampling and physical alignment.

intro.p: Mark the events of a trigger-like condition and walk through them. The first set of a source, level or slope adds Search 1 like the Add rail does. Studio has up to three searches: `:SEARch<n>:...` with `<n>` 1 to 3 is Search n, and without a number the command is of Search 1 (`STATe` and `MODE` are the same with any number; `VALue` takes none). The first set of `:SEARch2:EDGE:SOURce` adds Search 2; `:SEARch2:EVENt` goes to an event of Search 2 and makes it the selected search of the screen, the other commands leave the screen's choice alone. A search of Studio is of one of seven types, `EDGE`, `PULSe`, `SLOPe`, `TIMeout`, `RUNT`, `WINDow` and `BUS`, with the settings the trigger has for that type under the same names (`:SEARch:PULSe:WHEN` as `:TRIGger:PULSe:WHEN`). A `BUS` search has no source and no levels: it marks the packets of the active decoder (the one the Decode menu edits, which must be on) that the bus trigger's condition accepts, at the end of each packet, found by the decoder's own `ModuleInfo::trigger_match` (a frame, an ID or address, data, an error); `:SEARch:BUS:WHEN` and `:SEARch:BUS:VALue` are `:TRIGger:BUS:WHEN` and `:TRIGger:BUS:VALue`. A search has one set of settings, as the trigger has: a set under a type makes the search of that type, a query answers the setting whatever the type is, and `:SEARch:MODE` changes the type alone. The events are found in the samples by the software trigger, with a hysteresis of a tenth of a division. The events of the decoders have their own commands in decode.
Menu location: Decode and bus > Mark events, Search (type, source, slope or polarity, levels, 50 %, time condition, from / to trigger, event, event list, save events, remove).

intro.p: Protocol decoders: the `:DECode:` subtree edits the selected decoder slot, `:BUS<n>:` addresses decoder n directly (the decoder the menu edits stays the same afterwards), and `:BUS:LANE:` is the plot bus (I2C lane). Protocol-specific rows exist only for their protocol: an option the protocol does not have is -224. Decoder parameters take the option text of the menu row, and the query answers it in capitals. A decoder on channels reads the samples the acquisition kept when those are finer than the screen record (up to 262144 points per line while running, 4 M when stopped), so `:DECode:EVENts?` and `:BUS<n>:DATA?` can list events of the whole record, also outside the screen. A UART character the record starts inside is not listed, nor the ones behind it until its bits can be read in one way only; in peak detect, roll and above 1 M points it reads the 3600 points of the screen. The events of a decoder can also be searched by the type `BUS` of search. Reference sources may be used as roles if their native intervals overlap in physical time; no synthetic LA input is invented for a reference.
Menu location: Decode and bus (Protocol, Source / clock / CS, Threshold, Format, Events pane, protocol parameters, Plot bus, Save events).
Part of the SCPI reference.

intro.p: A generator beside the scope, on the USB-A port (USBTMC, no computer) or on the LAN. These commands name its model and where it is, connect to it, and switch a sine on. The Bode sweep with Generator = External sends through the same connection (bode.md); a sweep that finds none opens one for itself and closes it at its end.

A model with an error query (the OWON DGE) is asked after every command: what it refuses is shown on the screen, and a Bode sweep ends with it. While a Bode sweep steps the generator, the commands that would change the generator or its connection answer -221.
How the models are known: docs/extgen.md. The OWON DGE on the USB-A port of the scope is not yet verified on hardware.

intro.p: SIM generates a synthetic high-speed signal into a reference slot. The knob settings apply on the next `:SIM:PLAY ON`. A candidate replaces accepted data only when its trigger qualifies, Auto permits fallback, or Force is requested. Supported PRBS orders: 7, 9, 13, 15, 23, 31.

Run simulation mode on the screen is `:SIM:PLAY ON`: it plays the signal the knobs describe. The references that are shown (a loaded file, a signal added to a slot) are played from the screen with Play references, which has no command.
Part of the SCPI reference.

intro.p: Save and load setups, waveforms, screenshots and the fast-frame history, and fetch what was saved. A relative path of a save is taken in the save folder. The save folder is the USB stick when one is in (`:SAVE:DESTination`), else the scope's local folder, which is in memory and empty again after a power cycle: fetch a file with `:MMEMory:DATA?` or save to a stick to keep it. Setup slots are kept on the card. `*SAV` and `*RCL` (see common) and the setup block `:SYSTem:SETup` (see system) are the same setup files.

Menu location: Storage (Save to, Setup slot, Save setup, Recall setup, Save setup to file, Load setup from file, Save waveform, Fast-frame save / load, Save session, Load session, Save screenshot, Save setup as SCPI, SCPI recorder, Run SCPI file). Save setup as SCPI writes the lines of `:SYSTem:SETup:SCPI?` to a file. SCPI recorder writes what is set at the scope as commands while it is on and saves them as a file when it is switched off (`:SYSTem:RECorder:STATe`). Run SCPI file runs a file of commands on this scope: a recording, a setup saved as commands, or lines written by hand. The scope lists the `.scpi` files where Storage saves, the newest first; the desktop app asks with its Open dialog. The lines are run like a client's, one command a frame; a line that waits for an operation (`*OPC?`) is waited for, for at most 30 s; comment lines (`#`) are no commands. While a file runs the row reads Stop SCPI file. At the end the screen says how many commands were run, and the first one that was refused if any was; those errors do not reach a client: its error queue, event status and last error are as they were. A file sets the scope up, runs it and saves into the save folder, and no more (ADR 0033): refused from a file, and said as refused with -203, are a command with `CONFIRM` (the word would be the author's and not yours), every `:UI:` command that is not a query (a file does not press the screen), every `:SYSTem:` command that is not a query except `:SYSTem:SET`, `:SYSTem:SETup` and the ones a setup is written with (`:SYSTem:LOCK`, `:SYSTem:AOUTput`, `:SYSTem:PIPeline`, `:SYSTem:LOG:INTerval`), `:CALibrate:STARt`, `:MMEMory:DELete`, and a save or load whose file name is an absolute path or steps up with `..`: a file names files of the save folder. The rest of the file runs. A file saved by an editor with a byte order mark, or with CR LF or CR line ends, runs; a link or anything else that is not a regular file is not read. There is no command for this row: a client sends the lines itself.

In the menu, a row that writes a file asks for its name first and a row that reads one asks which file (ADR 0029): the on-screen keyboard and a list of the folder on the scope, the Save As and Open dialogs on the desktop build. The setup slots do not ask; Save setup to file and Load setup from file are `:SAVE:SETup` and `:LOAD:SETup` with a path. A command never asks: a path it is given is used as given, and without one it takes the next free name (a save) or the newest numbered file (a load), as the table says. A setup saved by name from the menu goes to the stick when files go there, else beside the slots (on the scope `/oos/setups`); `:LOAD:SETup` loads it by its full path.
Part of the SCPI reference.

intro.p: `:SYSTem:SET <key> = <value>` writes a key of the setup file on the live settings; `:SYSTem:GET? <key>` reads it. It is the setup schema: an escape hatch for tests and for the few settings that have no header. Where a header exists (the "Equivalent header" column), use that; the headers are in the group pages. The file written by Save setup and returned by `:SYSTem:SETup?` is the same list as `key = value` lines (`#` starts a comment), and `*SAV` / `*RCL` use the same files. `:SYSTem:SETup:SCPI?` writes the same setup as commands: for a key it uses the headers of the Equivalent header column where the table of `ui/src/scpi/setupscpi.rs` has them (a test keeps this column and that table the same), and a `:SYSTem:SET` line for the others.

ul: Values: booleans `true`/`false`, numbers in base units, enumerations as the Rust variant name (`Dc`, `Rise`, `Auto`), lists separated by blanks.
A key that is not in the list is rejected with -224 after the fact. Some keys are only written when they differ from their default and are marked optional.
Keys that carry a number are written with it (`ch2.vdiv`); here that number is `<n>`.
The Default column is the value of the default model (the Default setup), as `:SYSTem:SETup?` writes it; a dash means the key is optional or only written for a non-default state.
A source in a setup key is its token: the channel number (`1` is CH1) or `R1`; `-` or `off` is none.
Some rows describe several keys with one text where the original description was shared; the keys are listed in the first column in the same order as the values of the second.
